lots.guide_summary: Close entries run $15 to $500 (all AUD, every page opened). SOLD: 11 close results, Feb 2025 to Sep 2026, $50 to $500 hammer or Invaluable sold amount, median about $110 with the E J Ainger table counted once; plain mahogany tables made $50 to $300, walnut-topped ones $80 to $500. The only Tasmanian close sale is Gowans $50 after three passes. UNSOLD: 8 close tables passed in at last bids of $15 to $260 (one Gowans pass shows no amount), and several only sold after repeated passes and estimate cuts. ASKING: none kept. Category guides (burr or inlaid walnut tops, three-legged or round tripod tables) sold $150 to $650 and do not set the range. Invaluable figures may or may not include premium. No currency conversion needed.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close SOLD in the last 24 months in similar condition is $50 (Vickers & Hoad 8 Mar 2026, and Gowans 26 Jun 2026). 50 / 1.22 = 40.98, round down to $40 hammer ($48.80 all-in with Armitage's 22% premium incl GST). Flip: likely resale about $110 hammer (median of the close SOLD set: 50, 50, 80, 95, 100, 120, 170, 300, 300, 500, counting the E J Ainger table once), less about 15% vendor commission (assumed, not verified, $16.50) and $0 postage (local auction resale, buyer collects) = $93.50; 93.50 / 2.44 = 38.3, round down to $35. Flip margin is thin: tables of this kind passed in repeatedly at Gowans, Woodlands, Leonard Joel, Lawsons and Aalders. Pickup only from 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay; inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: Form and period are clear and 11 close SOLD records were opened (10 Invaluable pages plus a Gowans record with photos), but furniture of this kind carries no mark to read, the top timber and tilt action are unconfirmed, and the refinished top, edge split and mismatched frieze need a look in person.
lots.score_reason: A real mid-Victorian carved loo table, but close Australian sales mostly run $50 to $300 (median about $110) and lot 390 has a refinished top, an edge split and a frieze that does not match. Worth about $80 to $200, so 5.
lots.key_photo_findings: Three photos checked with enlarged crops. One-piece oval top with a moulded edge in a straight-grained reddish timber, refinished with a patchy orange-brown polish, small dark spots, and a short break or join in the edge moulding at the front (photo 3). The frieze is a much paler honey-coloured figured timber with a visible vertical joint, unlike the top and base, so it may be a different or replacement timber, or the top has been stained darker. Ring-turned and gadrooned baluster column with a dark collar; four leaf-carved, scroll-shouldered cabriole legs ending in scroll toes; white ceramic castors on all four legs. No underside, tilt catch, label or stamp shown. At 117 x 87 cm it is smaller than most comparables (134 to 154 cm long).
lots.condition: Base looks sound and complete, carving crisp, all four castors present. Top refinished, patchy and faded, with small dark marks and a split or join in the front edge moulding. Frieze timber does not match the top or base. Tilt mechanism, column joint and underside not shown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Does the top tilt and does the catch work, and is the column firm with no wobble or repaired legs? What timber is the top, solid or veneered, and is the pale frieze original or a replacement (if the table is Australian cedar, blackwood or Huon pine rather than English mahogany it would interest local buyers more)? Is the mark at the front edge a crack or an old join? Are all four ceramic castors original and turning?
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped as not the same item: Gowans 435935 ($200 card table) and its pass 434558; Gowans 375464 ($260), 418389 ($625) and 440826 ($55), round tops on triform platform bases; Gowans 407198 ($80), 399471 ($35) and 432860 ($65), plain round tilt-tops on tripod legs; McKenzies $600 (round, 142 cm) and $950 (round burr walnut with marquetry, 92 cm); Vickers & Hoad $480 (17 May 2026) and its $320 pass (15 Feb 2026), a Regency-style rounded-rectangular breakfast table on plain splayed legs with brass paw castors; Albion $250 (24 Sep 2026), a round cedar and mahogany tilt-top on a platform base; Moorabool $200 pass (2 Nov 2024), a burr walnut four-column table titled NR yet passed, category guide only. Gowans 403348 (pass) folded into the Gowans 404944 note as the same table. All 10 UK results (7 SOLD, 3 UNSOLD; Cheffins, Lyon & Turnbull x2, Adam Partridge, Andrew Smith x3, Elstob, Claydon, Lacy Scott & Knight) dropped: overseas, mostly rosewood or burr or inlaid walnut, and the Australian evidence is ample. All 4 ASKING entries dropped: three 1stDibs dealer asks (GBP 1,250 rosewood loo table, GBP 1,350 burr walnut loo table, GBP 450 rectangular bobbin-turned tilt-top) and South Perth Antiques A$1,595 (a round mahogany platform-base table, marked SOLD at an unknown price) are not the same item. Prices, dates and kinds of all re-opened entries matched the researcher, except that the researcher missed the lot's stated size and the Moorabool condition note (one castor missing).

lots.what_it_is: Box lot (Armitage title: 'BOX OF 1980'S BIRD FIGURINES, SHELLEY VASE ETC') carried by a Shelley (Longton, England) hand-painted Art Deco butterfly vase: footed ovoid vase with a black neck and shoulder, white dot-and-dash borders and purple, green and white butterflies over a pale yellow body. Base: green printed shield 'MADE IN SHELLEY ENGLAND', printed 'Rd 680712' (a 1921 registration, so a 1920s piece), hand-painted pattern number 8433 (Potteries Auctions catalogued an '8433 pattern pair of small vases' on 8 Mar 2024: https://www.invaluable.com/auction-lot/a-mixed-collection-of-shelley-items-to-include-8685-floral-decorated-small-vase-8433-pattern-pair-of-825-c-1AD44B7B5E) and a second hand-painted number read as 801 or 108 depending on orientation. Height not stated, roughly 18 to 22 cm by eye. The rest of the box is ordinary: two tall pink 1980s swan or flamingo figurines, a small blue jasper-style dish, a fluted posy bowl and two cream jugs with rose sprays.

lots.working: Keep: lowest close SOLD inside 24 months in similar condition is $40 (Theodore Bruce lot 164, 21 Jun 2026, 24 cm butterfly vase with wear only). 40 / 1.22 = 32.8, round down to $30 hammer ($36.60 all-in with 22% premium incl GST). Flip: likely resale about $50 (median of the five in-window close SOLD: 40, 45, 50, 86, 90), less about 15% selling fees ($7.50, assumed) and $0 outbound postage (local auction resale, or postage charged to the buyer) = $42.50; 42.50 / 2.44 = 17.4, round down to $15. lots.confidence_reason: Shelley shield mark, Rd 680712 and pattern 8433 are read in the photos and five in-window close SOLD pages were opened, but none is the same shape and colourway (black-ground or squat butterfly vases), and the height and close condition are not known.
lots.score_reason: A genuine hand-painted Shelley butterfly vase from a 1921 design, but recent Australian sales of the same series run $40 to $90 and the rest of the box is worth little. About $40 to $90, so 4.
lots.key_photo_findings: Three photos checked; base marks enlarged and rotated. Green printed shield 'MADE IN SHELLEY ENGLAND', printed 'Rd 680712' and hand-painted '8433' are clear; the second hand-painted number reads 801 or 108 depending on which way it is read. The vase is hand-painted: black neck and shoulder with white dot-and-dash borders and purple, green and white butterflies over a pale yellow body on a short foot. No chips, cracks or restoration visible; one tiny dark speck in the yellow; light staining and wear on the unglazed foot rim. Other pieces: two tall pink bird figurines with gilt beaks, a blue jasper-style pin dish, a fluted bowl with posies and gilt foot, two cream jugs with rose sprays; their bases are not shown.
lots.condition: Vase looks good from the photos: no visible chips, cracks or crazing, light wear to the foot rim only. Other pieces look intact from the front.
lots.question_for_armitage: How tall is the Shelley vase, and are there any chips, hairline cracks or touched-up paint on the rim, butterflies or foot (worth checking under a light at the viewing)? Do the jugs, bowl or figurines carry any maker's marks?

lots.what_it_is: Six cartons (Armitage title: '6 BOXES OF HO,00 GUAGE MODEL TRAIN, ROLLING STOCK TRACK ETC') of mostly 1965 to 1971 era Tri-ang Hornby 00 gauge in red 'Tri-ang Hornby' window boxes, with a little Lima HO. About 10 boxed items (Freightliner container flat, BR green parcels van, car transporter with three cars, BR maroon Mk1 coach, BR green electric loco, a green steam loco with a partly legible 'R.33?' label, purple bogie wagon, brake van and wagons, Esso tankers including one in a Lima HO box, a yellow-box accessory set with logs); loose locos (green 0-6-0T, black BR 2-6-4T numbered 80033 or similar, a GWR green single-driver loco with maroon frames and tender that looks like the Tri-ang 'Lord of the Isles', a spare chassis); a red and yellow crane wagon, four GWR clerestory coaches, two green coach shells; a boxed turntable with points and a controller, a big tray of track and points, plastic girder bridge and station parts, a tunnel, Tri-ang catalogues and a Hornby Dublo instruction booklet. Untested.

lots.working: There is no sale of a lot this size, so the lowest lot-scale close SOLD is used as a conservative floor (lot 396 holds more than either close lot): $160 (Gowans 411924, a single carton). 160 / 1.22 = 131.1, round down to $130 hammer ($158.60 all-in with 22% premium incl GST). The small boxed groups ($51 to $90) are treated as component guides, not same-item sales, because lot 396 holds roughly double their boxed content plus the loose locos, coaches, turntable and track. Flip: likely resale taken conservatively as $240 hammer (Gowans 411941, a smaller lot of the same era), less about 15% vendor commission and lot fee (assumed, not verified, about $36) and $0 postage (local auction resale, buyer collects) = $204; 204 / 2.44 = 83.6, round down to $80. Indicative sum of parts if split (guide only): about 10 boxed pieces with 2 boxed locos, like two $51 to $90 groups ($120 to $170), plus loose locos, coaches, turntable and track like the $160 to $240 cartons, about $280 to $400 hammer before fees.
